An electronic document generated on the GST portal for the movement of goods worth over ₹50,000. It ensures faster movement of goods and tracks tax compliance.
An oil refining nation or facility that can rapidly adjust its export destinations and product mix to balance sudden global supply or demand shocks.
Running a business independently without the financial, operational, or strategic backing of a parent company, partner, or merged corporate entity.

A category of investors in public offerings (like IPOs) who bid for shares worth more than two lakh rupees, but are not Qualified Institutional Buyers. This often includes high-net-worth individuals and corporate bodies.

Large institutional investors like mutual funds, foreign portfolio investors, and insurance companies who are deemed to have the expertise and financial muscle to evaluate investment opportunities without extensive regulatory oversight.

A group of 17 chemical elements essential for high-tech products like smartphones, electric vehicles, and defense systems. They are critical for modern industries and often monopolized by a few countries.

term: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
definition: A subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India that provides deposit insurance, protecting bank depositors if a bank fails. Currently, it covers deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.
Bad loans that remain on a bank's books after it has made provisions (set aside funds) for potential losses. Lower Net NPAs indicate better asset quality and financial health for banks.

A non-binding set of principles guiding civil space exploration and use of the Moon, Mars, comets, and asteroids. Led by NASA, it promotes peaceful, transparent, and sustainable space activities among signatory nations.
A fund created by the RBI where banks must transfer balances of accounts that have remained inactive for 10 or more years.
The difference in value between the crude oil a refinery purchases and the wholesale price of the petroleum products it produces from that oil.
A derivatives market where investors trade contracts to buy or sell financial assets at a set price in the future, often used for speculation or hedging.
Premium-quality corporate real estate characterized by excellent infrastructure, prime locations, professional management, and modern amenities.
An independent assessment of a country's creditworthiness, indicating its overall level of risk and ability to pay back national debt.
The integration of artificial intelligence systems into physical robotic bodies, allowing them to interact and perform labor in real-world environments.
A supervised, controlled testing environment established by regulators where technology companies can trial innovative products under relaxed compliance rules.
A highly regulated, licensed custodian responsible for the physical safekeeping, auditing, and insurance of physical commodities backing digital financial assets.
A preliminary registration document filed by a company with SEBI before its IPO, containing detailed financial, operational, and structural details.
A system where a financial platform holds only a portion of its outstanding liabilities in actual physical assets, exposing investors to default risks.
Dedicated offshore facilities established by multinational corporations to handle technology development and research, driving corporate office demand in India.
An account that has seen no customer-initiated transactions for over two years, requiring banks to classify its funds separately.
The formal process of declaring a legal beneficiary who will inherit the financial assets in an account if the owner passes away.
The secure storage of physical precious metals like gold and silver in certified, high-security facilities under strict custody rules.
The business practice of outsourcing operations to a nearby country with similar time zones, rather than a distant offshore location.
When an investment offer, like an IPO or a fund, receives more bids or commitments from investors than the number of shares or capital being offered. It signals strong market demand.
Money held in bank accounts that has remained inactive for ten years or more, where the owner has not initiated any transaction or communication with the bank regarding the account.
Debt instruments issued by a borrower, in this case an Indian entity, but denominated and traded in US dollars. These are typically aimed at international investors.
The ability of an organization or system to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises on its cyber resources.
Financial contracts, such as futures and options, whose value is linked to and derived from an underlying asset like stocks, commodities, or currencies.
Taxes paid directly to the government by individuals or corporations, primarily consisting of personal income tax and corporate tax.
A corporate restructuring strategy where a conglomerate splits off one or more of its business units into separate, independent entities.
High-risk financial transactions focused on profiting from short-term price fluctuations rather than building long-term investment value.

A category of urban transportation that involves lightweight, often electric-powered vehicles like e-bikes and scooters. It's used for short-distance travel, especially for last-mile connectivity in cities.
A type of artificial intelligence that can produce new content, like text, images, or code, by learning from existing data, rather than just analyzing or classifying it.
A financial instrument used to lock in an exchange rate for a future transaction, helping businesses protect themselves against currency fluctuations.
An advanced form of artificial intelligence capable of creating new content like text, images, or code, rather than just analyzing existing data.
A digital form of a country's fiat currency, issued and backed by its central bank, designed to complement physical cash and traditional bank deposits.
The total loss reported by a parent company and all its subsidiaries, presented as a single financial figure.

A large corporation made up of several different, often unrelated, businesses. Think of it as a parent company owning many diverse companies across various industries, like manufacturing, technology, and retail.

A digital form of a country's fiat currency, issued and backed by the central bank. Unlike cryptocurrencies, it is centralized and directly controlled by monetary authorities, aiming for safer and more efficient payments.
An industrial plant where crude oil is processed and refined into more useful petroleum products like gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. Refineries are crucial for meeting energy demands.

A government body established under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, in India. Its purpose is to protect home-buyers, ensure transparency in real estate transactions, and regulate the sector's promoters and agents.

The international market price for aluminium, a base metal, influenced by factors like supply (production, refinery output), demand (manufacturing, construction), inventory levels, energy costs, and geopolitical events affecting trade routes or major producers.
A state where one nation's essential supply chains rely heavily on another's specialized processing infrastructure rather than its own raw reserves.
Integrating financial services directly into non-financial platforms, like offering instant credit options inside a retail or telecom app.
The threat of substantial financial or operational disruption that an organization faces when a highly influential leader abruptly departs.
The process of turning physical assets like warehouses or roads into tradeable, liquid public securities to raise large-scale capital.
Premium industrial logistics space built with modern height clearance, heavy floor loading capacity, and high-tech automated inventory systems.
The markup or profit margin a bank charges on top of its benchmark interest rate when pricing a loan for a borrower.
A trade pact between nations that reduces tariffs on a specific list of goods, being less comprehensive than a free trade agreement.
A measure of inflation that excludes highly volatile price categories, such as food and energy, to reveal long-term cost trends.
A government financial grant that covers a percentage of a company's upfront capital expenditure spent on building factories or infrastructure.
A corporate program where a company uses its cash reserves to purchase shares back from its employees, providing them with real-money liquidity.
A business model where a platform connects commercial buyers with manufacturing units to produce industrial parts and custom goods.
An interest rate that banks and other lenders must link their floating-rate loans to, such as the RBI's repo rate, making loan pricing more transparent and responsive to policy changes.
A measure of sales growth for retail locations that have been open for a year or more, excluding new store openings. It indicates the health of existing operations.
A range of electromagnetic frequencies used primarily for satellite communications, weather radar, and military tracking, known for its high data capacity.
An online business model where the platform acts as an active intermediary, guaranteeing quality, delivery, and payments instead of just matching buyers and sellers.
A unique 12-digit number assigned to salaried employees in India, allowing them to manage and port their retirement savings across different employers.
A business strategy where a company minimizes its ownership of physical assets, choosing instead to outsource manufacturing operations to specialized partners.
A loan where the interest rate changes periodically based on a benchmark rate, meaning your monthly payments can go up or down.
Any information that, if made public, is likely to materially affect the price of a company's securities, and is not generally available.
A formal order from a regulatory body requiring an individual or entity to explain why a particular action should not be taken against them.
A financial institution that provides loans against gold collateral but does not hold a banking license or accept public deposits.
The total profit of a parent company and all its subsidiaries, combined. It gives a full picture of the entire group's financial performance.
Debt securities issued by companies that are offered and sold outside the United States, usually to non-U.S. persons, to avoid certain U.S. registration requirements.

An interest rate regime where banks link loan rates to an external benchmark, such as the RBI repo rate or government treasury bill yields, aimed at faster and more transparent interest rate transmission.
The additional interest percentage charged by a lender above a benchmark rate, covering the bank's operational costs, risk premium, and profit margin. It can change independently of the benchmark.

When a country's total exports of goods, services, and transfers are greater than its total imports. This indicates the nation is earning more from the world than it is spending, typically strengthening its currency and external financial position.

A large-scale computing infrastructure specifically designed and built to support the training, deployment, and operation of complex Artificial Intelligence models. It typically involves massive clusters of high-performance GPUs and specialized software.

A protectionist tariff that a domestic government imposes on foreign imports that it believes are priced below fair market value. It's meant to protect domestic industries from 'dumping' by foreign competitors.
A dedicated stock exchange segment designed to facilitate fundraising for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) by offering simpler listing and compliance requirements compared to the main board.
The total value of shares issued by a company to its shareholders after an initial public offering (IPO) or other share issuance, representing the capital contributed by owners.
The amount of money a company has received from shareholders in exchange for shares of stock. It represents the capital legally invested in the company by its owners.
The difference in yield between a riskier bond and a risk-free government benchmark of the same maturity, reflecting the issuer's perceived default risk.
The investment risk associated with state-owned or state-backed companies, which are viewed by global markets as nearly as safe as the national government itself.
A regulatory framework that allows banks to link pre-approved credit lines to UPI accounts, enabling users to pay merchants using borrowed funds.
A specialized microprocessor designed specifically to accelerate artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms locally on a device.
A long-term agreement between a buyer and seller that specifies fixed quantities and pricing mechanisms for commodities over a set period.
A key metric in the insurance industry, representing the sum of 100% of new regular premiums and 10% of single premiums. It helps measure the performance of new business.
An important profitability measure in the insurance sector, estimating the present value of future profits expected from new policies sold during a specific period.
The per-unit price of a mutual fund or pension scheme. It is calculated by dividing the total value of assets in the fund, minus liabilities, by the number of units outstanding.
An investment class consisting of capital that is not listed on a public exchange, used to buy or invest directly in private companies.
An assessment of the creditworthiness of a borrower or debt instrument, indicating the likelihood of default on loan payments.
A direct financial grant provided by a government to a private business to cover a portion of its capital setup or building costs.
A type of debt security that takes precedence over other unsecured debt in the event of liquidation, meaning holders of senior notes are paid before other unsecured creditors.
Financial instruments issued by a company to its promoters or select investors, giving them the right to buy shares at a predetermined price within a specific period, often used for capital raising.

The price at which new shares or other securities are offered to investors during an initial public offering (IPO) or other primary market issuance. It's the price at which investors first buy the security from the company.

A branch of a bank located in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) like GIFT City, India, that can conduct banking activities with non-residents in foreign currencies, offering a global financial hub environment.

An investor deemed financially sophisticated and capable of handling higher investment risks. They often meet specific income or asset thresholds and can participate in investment opportunities not available to the general public.
A nuclear reactor that generates more fissile material (fuel) than it consumes. This technology is crucial for countries like India with limited uranium reserves but abundant thorium.
A Proton Exchange Membrane electrolyzer is a device used to produce green hydrogen by efficiently splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity from renewable sources.
The total sum of all money that people and entities have placed into bank accounts, including savings, current, and fixed deposits, across a bank or the entire banking system.
The formal rules and procedures used by the market regulator (SEBI) to allow entities that have violated regulations to resolve their cases without lengthy litigation, often by paying a penalty.

These are unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) or drones that can 'loiter' or wait over a target area for an extended period, searching for targets, and then attack once a target is identified. They combine reconnaissance capabilities with precision strike abilities.

A corporate guarantee is a promise by one company (the guarantor) to cover the debt or obligations of another company (the borrower) if the borrower defaults. It reduces the risk for lenders but creates a contingent liability for the guarantor.

This is a mechanism used by stock exchanges to determine the closing price of securities, typically by collecting buy and sell orders within a specific window at the end of trading. It helps in reducing price volatility at market close.
A tactical unmanned weapon system, also called a suicide drone, designed to hover over an area to locate and strike targets by crashing into them.
The core measure of a bank or financial institution's financial strength, consisting primarily of common stock and disclosed reserves.
An expedited defense procurement mechanism used to acquire critical operational equipment quickly during urgent security requirements.

term: MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate)
definition: The minimum interest rate below which a bank is not permitted to lend, except in specific cases allowed by the central bank, calculated based on the incremental cost of funds.
A retail store dedicated solely to selling products of a single brand, managed directly by the company or through a franchise agreement to maintain brand control.
Debt financing provided by non-bank financial institutions to companies, often structured as customized bilateral loans rather than publicly traded bonds.

Also known as 'suicide drones' or 'kamikaze drones,' these are aerial weapons that can loiter around a target area for an extended period, detecting threats and then striking them by crashing into the target itself.
An inflation index that measures the change in the price of goods sold and traded in bulk by wholesale businesses, reflecting industrial cost pressures.

A fraudulent investment operation where the operator pays returns to earlier investors with money taken from later investors, rather than from actual profits. It eventually collapses when new money stops coming in.
A metric showing how much of a bank's funds raised through deposits are being used to extend loans, reflecting banking system liquidity.

The total value of goods sold over a certain period through a customer-to-customer or e-commerce platform, before subtracting fees, returns, or expenses. It indicates the total volume of sales activity.

The amount of capital a bank or financial institution has relative to its risk-weighted assets. It ensures banks have enough funds to absorb potential losses and remain stable, protecting depositors' money.
The total amount of tax, including surcharges and cesses, that an individual or entity is liable to pay to the government on their income or assets. It represents the final tax burden.

A farming management concept that uses advanced technologies like GPS, sensors, and drones to observe, measure, and respond to variability in crops and soil, optimizing resource use and maximizing yields.
A retrospective tax is a tax imposed on transactions or income that occurred in the past, before the law imposing the tax was enacted. This can create uncertainty for businesses and investors.
The percentage of the total labor force that is unemployed but actively seeking employment and willing to work. It's a key indicator of economic health.
Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) scheme, allowing Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to hold term deposits in foreign currencies in India, often used by RBI to attract foreign exchange.
Entities like stockbrokers, mutual funds, and depositories that facilitate transactions and services in the securities market, connecting investors with investments.
In Artificial Intelligence, a large AI model trained on a vast dataset that can be adapted to a wide range of diverse tasks, serving as a base for many applications.
Refers to the infrastructure and operations involved in supplying natural gas to homes, industries, and vehicles (CNG) within specific geographical areas.
The first significant round of venture capital financing a startup receives after its initial seed funding, typically used to scale operations and develop its product or service.
A list issued by India's Ministry of Defence specifying defence items, components, or sub-systems that can no longer be imported and must instead be procured from domestic manufacturers.
The highly complex and capital-intensive process of manufacturing integrated circuits (computer chips) on silicon wafers in specialized factories known as fabrication plants or 'fabs'.
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth measures the increase in the value of all goods and services produced in a country over a specific period, indicating economic expansion.

United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) approval is a regulatory clearance required for pharmaceutical products to be marketed and sold in the United States, signifying safety and efficacy.
A payments bank is a special type of bank in India that can accept deposits up to ₹2 lakh, facilitate remittances, and offer debit cards, but cannot issue loans or credit cards.
EXIM refers to Export and Import operations, encompassing all activities related to international trade, including logistics, documentation, and compliance for goods moving across borders.

A mutual fund is a professionally managed investment fund that pools money from many investors to purchase securities like stocks, bonds, and other assets. It offers diversification and professional management.
Duty-free imports refer to goods brought into a country without being subjected to customs duties or tariffs. This typically makes imported products cheaper for domestic consumers and businesses.
CIC refers to the amount of physical currency (banknotes and coins) that is held by the public and is not in the vaults of commercial banks. It's a measure of the cash being used in the economy.
A regulatory rule stating that if an agency fails to approve or reject a business license application within a set timeframe, the license is automatically considered granted.
A global business strategy where companies diversify their manufacturing operations by establishing plants outside China to hedge against geopolitical risks.
Money spent by private businesses to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets like factories and machinery, driving economic growth.
An increase in corporate profits achieved primarily through internal cost-cutting and efficiency measures rather than an actual increase in sales volume.
The percentage by which a company's stock price rises above its initial public offering (IPO) price when it first begins trading on the exchange.
An agreement between two parties to exchange principal and interest payments in different currencies, used by central banks to manage liquidity and foreign reserves.
The official agreement of the President of India that turns a bill passed by both houses of Parliament into the legally binding law of the land.
A foreign currency non-resident bank account swap facility used by central banks to manage domestic dollar liquidity and stabilize currency exchange rates.
National regulations that govern or restrict the transport of goods or passengers between two ports within the same country by foreign-registered vessels.
The percentage of a country's total working-age population that is actively employed, serving as a key indicator of real labor market strength.
A regulatory policy where an application is automatically treated as approved if the governing authority fails to respond within a legally defined timeframe.
Processed milk items like cheese, paneer, and yogurt that undergo advanced manufacturing to command higher retail prices and yield superior profit margins compared to liquid milk.
The minimum number of members required to be present at a meeting to make the proceedings valid and decisions legally binding. Without it, decisions are typically not legitimate.

The process of developing and producing goods or services domestically instead of importing them, often driven by government policy to boost local industry and self-reliance, especially in critical sectors.

A missile that follows a ballistic trajectory to deliver one or more warheads to a predetermined target. They are powered for only a short initial phase of flight, with the rest unpowered and following gravity.

Money flowing into a country, usually from foreign sources, for investment in its financial markets or real assets. These inflows can boost economic growth but also introduce volatility to exchange rates.
Build-Operate-Transfer; a public-private partnership model where a private firm constructs infrastructure, operates it to recover costs through fees, and later transfers it to the government.
A system that uses artificial intelligence and algorithms to analyze a borrower's financial data and instantly determine their creditworthiness and risk.
Funds transferred by foreign workers to their home countries, serving as a vital source of foreign exchange and household income for country of origin.

A model for public-private partnerships in infrastructure projects, particularly highways. The government pays a portion of the project cost upfront and the rest as annuities over time, sharing revenue and traffic risks.
A competitive process where companies submit proposals to develop and supply renewable energy, typically to government agencies or utilities, at a specific price and capacity.
Financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying asset, like stocks, bonds, or commodities. Common types include futures and options, used for hedging risk or speculation.

An Initial Public Offering (IPO) specifically for Small and Medium Enterprises. These companies list on a separate platform of stock exchanges (like BSE SME) with simplified regulations for fundraising.
A mandate by the RBI for banks to lend a specified portion of their funds to certain sectors deemed important for the overall economy, such as agriculture, education, and small businesses.

Financial contracts whose value is derived from the performance of an underlying stock market index, like the Nifty 50 or Sensex. They allow investors to bet on the future movement of an index without buying all its individual stocks.

Individuals or small businesses who lack sufficient credit history for traditional lenders to assess their creditworthiness. This often makes it difficult for them to access formal loans and financial services.

An investment strategy where fund managers allocate less capital to a specific asset, sector, or country than its representation in their benchmark index, reflecting a negative outlook or expectation of underperformance.

A provision in a contract or treaty ensuring that certain conditions will be met, often granting the right to compensation or other recourse if they are not. It adds a layer of security for the parties involved.

A robot designed to resemble the human body in shape, with a torso, head, two arms, and two legs. These robots are often used for research, personal assistance, or performing tasks in hazardous environments.

Money sent by foreign workers or residents back to their home countries. For India, remittances from Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are a significant source of foreign exchange and contribute to the national economy.

Financial activities that support environmental sustainability. This includes investments in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and other eco-friendly projects, aiming to address climate change and promote sustainable development.
Companies that are larger than small businesses but not yet large corporations, typically having annual revenues between ₹100 crore and ₹2,000 crore, attracting private equity investment.
A bilateral agreement between India and Bangladesh on sharing the waters of the Ganges River, crucial for agriculture and livelihoods in both countries, periodically reviewed.
A maximum quantity of a commodity (like sugar) that a producer or trader is permitted to hold in inventory at any given time, imposed by the government to prevent hoarding and manage prices.
The total amount of money a company has received from its shareholders in exchange for shares, representing the face value of shares that have been fully paid for by investors.

A specialized research and development facility focused on creating and improving cybersecurity solutions by leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies to detect and combat cyber threats.

A concept in international tax law that determines if a foreign company has a sufficient business presence in a country to be subject to corporate income tax there. AI-driven models challenge its traditional definition.

A designated area in a country that has different economic laws than the rest of the country. SEZs offer various incentives to businesses, like tax breaks and simplified labor laws, to attract investment and boost exports.
Individual investors who buy and sell securities for their personal accounts, rather than for an organization. They typically trade smaller amounts of money compared to institutional investors.
A principal piece of Indian legislation that governs labor relations, prescribing the legal framework for investigation and settlement of industrial disputes.
A legal document that grants authority to another person to act on one's behalf, authenticated electronically. This streamlines administrative processes and enhances efficiency.
Complex financial derivatives that allow traders to bet on the future price movements of an underlying asset without owning it directly. They are often used for speculation or hedging.

A special facility provided by a central bank, like the RBI, allowing banks to swap foreign currency for local currency at a favorable exchange rate, often to manage liquidity or encourage foreign capital inflows.

An FPI is an entity that invests in the financial assets of a country other than its own. These investments are 'portfolio' because they don't give the investor direct ownership or control over the company.
An MoA is a formal agreement between two or more parties, outlining their understanding and cooperation on a specific matter. It is often less formal than a treaty but still legally significant.

This refers to the production volume of eight key industries in India: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, and electricity. Their performance is a key economic indicator.

A legal document that grants one person (the agent) the authority to act on behalf of another person (the principal) in specific financial, legal, or medical matters. Digitally signed PoAs allow for electronic execution.
The process of increasing the acceptance of the Indian Rupee for international transactions, like trade and capital flows, reducing reliance on other currencies such as the US Dollar.

A central bank's policy position focused primarily on controlling inflation, often implying a readiness to raise interest rates or tighten money supply, even if it might slow economic growth. It prioritizes price stability.

The return an investor receives on a government bond. It moves inversely to bond prices. Higher yields mean lower bond prices, often signaling higher borrowing costs for the government and broader economy.

A set of labor laws in India that consolidates and amends laws relating to trade unions, industrial employment (standing orders), and industrial disputes, aiming to streamline regulations for businesses and workers.

A factory or plant dedicated to the design, manufacturing, assembly, and testing of semiconductor devices, which are critical electronic components used in everything from computers to smartphones and AI systems.
A group of experts or officials appointed by the government to investigate a specific issue, analyze its complexities, and propose recommendations for policy changes or reforms.
An account that a domestic bank holds on behalf of a foreign bank, allowing international transactions to be settled directly in the domestic currency.
Debt securities that carry a higher priority of repayment over other unsecured debts if a borrower defaults, typically offering lower risk for investors.
The eight foundational sectors of the economy—including steel, coal, and electricity—whose performance acts as a leading indicator of overall industrial health.
A refund of customs duties and taxes paid on imported raw materials that are subsequently used to manufacture goods for export.
A shared, government-backed digital network—like UPI or Aadhaar—that enables private and public entities to deliver essential digital services securely at national scale.
A vehicle whose operations, features, and user experience are primarily controlled and updated via software and internet connectivity rather than mechanical parts.
A direct tax levied on the purchase and sale of securities (like stocks, mutual funds, and derivatives) traded on a registered stock exchange.
Funds used by a company or government to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets such as property, plants, or infrastructure.
A mandatory verification process used by financial institutions to confirm the identity and address of their customers to prevent financial fraud.
A transaction settlement cycle where trade-related payments and stock transfers are fully completed within 24 hours of the trade execution date.
A global organization that builds and manages stock market indexes, which international funds use as blueprints to guide their investment allocations.
Financial assets, such as corporate loans and credit lines, managed on behalf of large organizations rather than individual retail customers.

A financial contract between two parties that locks in an interest rate for a future loan or deposit. It helps manage interest rate risk by fixing the rate for a specific period starting at a future date.

A monetary policy tool used by the RBI to manage daily liquidity in the banking system. It involves daily auctions for repo (borrowing) and reverse repo (lending) operations, helping banks meet their short-term cash needs.
A clearing mechanism where buy and sell trades are offset against each other, requiring only the final difference to be paid in cash.
The reduction in a mutual fund's overall returns caused by keeping a portion of its assets in low-yield cash instead of fully investing it.
The national economic policy of designing and manufacturing critical defense equipment domestically to replace costly foreign military imports.
An auction-based policy tool used by the central bank to absorb excess cash from commercial banks, helping control inflation and manage market liquidity.
The ratio of a loan amount to the appraised value of the asset securing the loan, determining the maximum cash a borrower can secure.
An accounting method where transactions are recorded when they occur rather than when cash is exchanged, providing a complete view of financial health.
The direct sale of corporate stocks or bonds to pre-selected institutional investors rather than publicly on the open stock exchange.
Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction. A tool used by the RBI to absorb temporary excess cash from the banking system, helping control short-term inflation and stabilize market rates.
A government-certified quality assurance system in India that officially verifies and stamps the purity of gold jewelry, protecting buyers from metal adulteration.
The total amount of financial investment or lending support a commercial bank provides to equity-related activities, such as buying stocks directly or lending to brokers.
An advanced engineering method of cooling server chips by circulating water or specialized liquids directly over them to dissipate intense heat.
A streamlined government regulatory system that allows businesses to obtain all necessary permits, land approvals, and licenses through a single unified portal.
A bookkeeping system where every financial transaction has equal and opposite effects in at least two different accounts.
A period of reduced investment activity where venture capitalists become highly selective, causing a sharp drop in startup valuations.
A debt security issued by a local government body to finance local capital expenditures like roads, water, and public schools.
An economic scenario where different sectors or income groups recover from a crisis at vastly different rates and trajectories.
A mechanism allowing banks to exchange foreign deposits for rupees with the central bank at a subsidized, stable exchange rate.
A GST feature allowing businesses to reduce their output tax liability by the amount of tax already paid on input purchases.
The annual rate of return an investor receives on a corporate debt security, which moves inversely to its market price.
The likelihood that a corporate borrower will fail to make required interest or principal payments on its debt.
A collaborative venture between a government agency and a private sector company to achieve a shared developmental goal.

A business model where a service provider is paid based on the measurable results or value delivered, rather than on the hours worked or resources spent. It incentivizes efficiency and client success.
A process in India allowing listed companies to raise capital by issuing equity shares, fully convertible debentures, or other securities to qualified institutional buyers.
A method for Indian listed companies to raise capital by selling shares or convertible securities to qualified institutional buyers, bypassing a more public and lengthy IPO process.
A medicine that contains two or more active ingredients in a single dosage form. These are common in many therapeutic areas but require strict regulatory oversight.
Individuals or entities registered to sell mutual fund schemes to investors. They play a crucial role in increasing financial literacy and market penetration.

A single medicine that contains two or more active drug ingredients. While some are beneficial, others are considered 'irrational' if the combination lacks scientific justification or poses unnecessary risks.
A system where drivers are charged a fee for using certain roads, especially in busy urban areas, during peak times. It aims to reduce traffic, pollution, and encourage public transport use.

An Exchange Traded Fund that primarily invests in physical gold or gold-related assets. Its units trade on stock exchanges, offering investors a liquid and cost-effective way to gain exposure to gold prices.

An acronym for 'Security and Growth for All in the Region,' it is India's strategic vision for the Indian Ocean region. It emphasizes cooperation, security, and inclusive development among regional nations.
Artificial intelligence systems designed to analyze and predict human actions, communication preferences, and decision-making patterns to personalize digital interactions.
A highly powerful network of interconnected computers, typically packed with advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), used to perform massive, complex calculations like training AI models.
A regulatory framework where an infrastructure asset, like a gas pipeline, must be shared equally among all competing companies to prevent duplicate construction and lower tariffs.

Not in Education, Employment, or Training. A macroeconomic metric tracking the proportion of the youth population that is completely disengaged from both the education system and the formal job market.
Artificial intelligence that is integrated directly with physical machines, sensors, and industrial systems to automate complex physical processes, as opposed to purely digital or virtual tasks.
A legal classification in United States immigration policy used to deny entry visas to foreign nationals who are deemed highly likely to depend on government welfare programs for subsistence.
India's strategic foreign policy framework, standing for Security and Growth for All in the Region, aimed at deepening maritime security and economic cooperation in the Indian Ocean.
Taxes imposed by a country on imports from another country as a direct response to tariffs previously placed on its own goods.
Online Bond Platform Provider, a SEBI-regulated digital portal that allows retail investors to buy and sell corporate debt securities directly.
The interest expenses and other borrowing costs incurred by a company to secure and service its loans and corporate debt.
A report issued by US FDA inspectors listing conditions at a manufacturing facility that could violate American drug safety and quality standards.
Financial arrangements where a central bank exchanges foreign currency for domestic currency with local banks at a discounted, highly favorable rate to boost forex reserves.
Community-based financial institutions owned and run by members, serving local small businesses, traders, and households in urban and semi-urban areas.
A digital intermediary registered with regulators that allows retail investors to buy and sell corporate debt securities online.
A military or economic response that does not match the scale or method of the initial attack but targets different vulnerabilities to inflict disproportionate damage.
A short-range wireless connectivity technology that enables devices like smartphones to securely transmit payment data to terminal readers with a single tap.
The migration of a corporate debt issuer's credit rating over time, indicating whether its risk of default has increased or decreased.
Bank accounts held by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) in foreign currency, offering stable, tax-exempt returns. They are a significant channel for attracting foreign currency into India.

Integrations of computation, networking, and physical processes, where embedded computers and communication networks monitor and control physical machinery, serving as the foundational infrastructure for smart manufacturing and modern factories.
A phase in the economic cycle where business performance, profitability, and investment flows recover sharply after hitting a temporary bottom or structural contraction.
An acronym for 'Not in Education, Employment, or Training', used by economists to measure the segment of the youth population that is completely idle and disconnected from the workforce.
The risk that the price of a fixed-income bond will fall as a result of an increase in interest rates, which is typically higher for longer-term bonds.
A vehicle that operates on an electric motor, powered by batteries, rather than an internal combustion engine, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and lowering emissions.

Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) are overseas entities that invest in a country's financial assets like stocks and bonds. Their investments are 'portfolio' because they're focused on financial gains, not controlling companies.

These are intermediaries proposed by SEBI to help retail investors buy and sell fixed-income securities, like bonds, more easily. They would operate through online platforms to increase market access.

This refers to the economic growth potential that can result from shifts in a country's population age structure, particularly when the share of the working-age population (15 to 64) is larger than the non-working-age share.
Investment made by entities in financial assets like stocks, bonds, and mutual funds in a foreign country, without aiming for controlling ownership or management influence.
A special scheme offered by a central bank (like RBI) to commercial banks, allowing them to swap foreign currency for local currency at a favorable, predetermined rate to attract forex inflows.

term: PNGRB (Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board)
definition: The Indian regulatory authority that oversees the infrastructure and operations related to refining, transporting, and distributing petroleum products and natural gas within the country.
Taxes imposed by a government on imported goods or services. Tariffs are used to influence trade flows, protect domestic industries, or as leverage in trade negotiations.

The entire range of activities and resources involved in creating, providing, and using space-related products and services, including satellite manufacturing, launch services, and ground applications.
The minimum amount of assets minus liabilities that a financial entity, like a stockbroker, must maintain to operate. This acts as a financial cushion against losses and protects clients.
The framework of policies, rules, and best practices designed to ensure that AI systems are developed and used responsibly, ethically, and securely, particularly in sensitive sectors like banking.
The actual amount of bad loans a bank has, calculated by subtracting the provisions it has set aside from its total defaults.
The percentage of bad loans that a bank has already covered by setting aside funds from its profits, reducing future default risks.
A dedicated, bulk-freight railway transport service deployed by the Indian government to rapidly move essential onion stocks to curb retail inflation.
A situation where a firm or individual has competing professional or personal interests, making it difficult to perform duties impartially.
The strategic process of expanding a nation's export markets and trading partners to reduce economic vulnerability to any single country.
The structural design and organization of cloud computing resources, databases, and software applications that run on the internet.

An investment strategy where an investor periodically transfers a fixed amount from one mutual fund scheme (usually a debt fund) to another (typically an equity fund) to average out costs and manage risk.
A state-controlled reserve of a commodity, such as agricultural crops, used to stabilize prices during times of shortage or high volatility.
Independent board members appointed to a governing body, such as the RBI Central Board, to represent commercial, industrial, or professional interests rather than the state.
The ratio of a bank's total loans to its total deposits. A high LDR means a bank is lending out most of the money it receives from deposits, indicating strong credit demand or tight liquidity.

A type of renewable energy project that combines intermittent sources like solar or wind with energy storage systems (like batteries) to provide a stable, predictable, and on-demand power supply to the grid.

An agreement between two or more countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs and other trade barriers on goods and services exchanged between them. The goal is to boost economic growth and foster closer economic ties.

In real estate, sales bookings represent the value of properties for which sales agreements have been signed during a specific period. It's an indicator of future revenue, even if the actual property handover and revenue recognition occur later.
A greenfield project is an infrastructure or industrial development built entirely from scratch on undeveloped land, as opposed to expanding or renovating an existing facility.
A type of compensation scheme where a portion of an employee's pay is directly tied to the achievement of specific performance targets or the company's financial results.
A transaction where existing shareholders sell their equity to other investors, meaning no new capital enters the company's treasury.
An economic index measuring the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers of goods and services.
A type of non-immigrant visa that allows foreign students to enter the United States to pursue full-time academic studies.
A metric that measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic service providers, capturing wholesale-level service inflation.
A foreign policy approach where a nation makes strategic decisions based purely on its own national interests, without being bound by alliances or external geopolitical pressures.

When a company or bank borrows money by issuing debt instruments (bonds) to investors in international markets, typically denominated in a foreign currency like US dollars, to diversify funding sources.

The process of adopting digital technology to improve an organization's processes, culture, and customer experiences to meet evolving market demands. In business, it often involves cloud, AI, and data analytics.

A framework used by regulators to assess and benchmark the strength, security, and recovery capabilities of information technology systems within critical financial market institutions against disruptions and cyber threats.
The premium at which an unlisted IPO share trades in the unofficial 'gray market' before its official listing. It's an informal indicator of investor demand and potential listing gains.
The entire network of companies, technologies, and infrastructure involved in the design, manufacturing, testing, and packaging of microchips, crucial for modern electronics.
Government initiatives and regulations aimed at promoting the domestic manufacturing, research, and development of semiconductors, critical components for electronic devices and advanced technology.

Reflagging is the process where a ship changes its country of registration, and thus the flag it sails under. For India, it means increasing the number of ships operating under the Indian flag to boost its national fleet.

A GPU is a specialized electronic circuit designed to rapidly manipulate and alter memory to accelerate image creation. In AI, GPUs are crucial for their parallel processing capabilities, making them highly efficient for training complex neural networks.

Food inflation refers to the sustained increase in the general price level of food items over a period. In India, it is a significant component of overall inflation and deeply impacts household budgets and purchasing power.
A national body that sets quality, safety, and performance standards for products in India. Certification ensures products meet these benchmarks, affecting both domestic goods and imports.
A cloud computing infrastructure designed to store and manage digital data entirely within a single nation's borders, protecting it from foreign jurisdictions and laws.
A fraudulent identity created by combining real stolen personal credentials, such as PAN cards, with fake details to bypass remote online verification systems.
A micro-warehouse closed to retail customers, dedicated entirely to fulfilling rapid delivery orders placed via quick-commerce applications.
A tax imposed by one country on imports from another country specifically to counter protective tariffs previously imposed by that nation.

Loans extended by banks to various sectors of the economy, excluding those for food procurement. It indicates credit flow to industries, services, and personal loans, reflecting broader economic activity.
A mechanism used for awarding infrastructure projects, particularly in power, where companies bid on the tariff (price) at which they will provide the service, fostering competition and efficiency.
A measure of the value of goods and services produced in an area, industry, or sector. It's often considered a better measure of economic activity than GDP, as it excludes net indirect taxes.

Funds deposited by Indian citizens residing abroad into Indian bank accounts. These deposits are a significant source of foreign exchange for India and contribute to the country's overall financial stability.

Hydrogen produced by splitting water using renewable energy sources like solar or wind power. It is considered a clean fuel with zero carbon emissions during production, crucial for decarbonizing heavy industries.

A specialized electronic circuit designed to rapidly manipulate and alter memory to accelerate the creation of images, videos, and increasingly, artificial intelligence computations. GPUs are critical for AI workloads.

Non-Resident External (NRE) deposits are rupee-denominated accounts opened by NRIs in India. Funds in these accounts are fully repatriable, meaning they can be freely transferred back to a foreign country.
The percentage of a bank's total deposits that it must maintain as cash reserves with the Reserve Bank of India. It helps control liquidity in the economy.

The percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that it must maintain in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or government securities. It ensures banks have enough liquid assets to meet short-term needs.
Missiles that use traditional high explosives, fragmentation, or kinetic impact to destroy targets. They do not carry nuclear, biological, or chemical warheads.
Earnings Before Interest and Taxes margin, a profitability ratio showing what percentage of revenue is left after covering operating costs, before accounting for interest and taxes.
A situation where short-term debt instruments have higher yields than long-term debt instruments, often seen as a predictor of an economic recession.
A temporary tool used by the RBI to absorb excess liquidity from banks by requiring them to hold an additional percentage of their new deposits as reserves, beyond the usual Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR).

When the owners (promoters) of a company use their shares in that company as collateral to borrow money, often to fund business expansion or personal investments. It can signal confidence or financial strain.
Transactions in which two or more companies combine through a merger or one company acquires another. It's a key strategy for growth, market expansion, and gaining new capabilities.
A trade policy tool that allows a specific quantity of a product to be imported at a reduced tariff rate (often zero), with imports exceeding that quota facing a higher tariff.

A proposed framework to channel long-term, 'patient capital' from one country to deep technology startups in another, fostering innovation in advanced fields like AI, quantum computing, and biotechnology.
A category of Indian Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) granted significant financial and operational autonomy by the government due to their strong financial performance and strategic importance.
Information related to water, including its distribution, movement, and properties within a region. Sharing this data helps manage shared rivers and prevent water-related disputes.
An advanced form of algorithmic trading that uses powerful computers to execute a vast number of orders at extremely high speeds, often exploiting tiny price discrepancies across markets.
A situation where two historically connected economic or political trends begin to move in different directions, such as rising trade despite frozen diplomatic relations.
The time delay between a system receiving an input (like spoken human words) and generating a response (like an AI's spoken answer).
A state-owned investment fund that invests a country's surplus money in global real estate, stocks, bond markets, and infrastructure.
A unit of power measurement, often used for engines that transmit power through a rotating shaft, like those in helicopters. It indicates the engine's output power available for propulsion.

The use of extremely powerful computing systems, often composed of thousands of interconnected processors, specifically optimized for artificial intelligence workloads like training complex machine learning models and processing vast datasets.
The practice where company founders use their personal equity shares as collateral to secure loans from banks or non-banking financial companies.
A demand from a lender for an investor to deposit additional money or securities so that the account is brought up to the minimum required value.
A major export grade of Russian oil, which has historically been sold to Indian refiners at a discount relative to global benchmarks like Brent crude.
A modern retail approach that seamlessly integrates the shopping experience across physical brick-and-mortar stores, websites, and mobile applications.
A temporary tool used by the central bank to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system by forcing banks to hold a higher percentage of their incremental deposits.
The difference between the highest price a buyer is willing to pay for an asset and the lowest price a seller is willing to accept, serving as a key measure of market liquidity.
A legal contract clause that frees parties from liability or obligation when an extraordinary, unavoidable event prevents them from fulfilling their duties.
A technology that merges data from multiple physical devices—like cameras, radar, and acoustic sensors—to generate a single, highly accurate security assessment.
A bilateral payment mechanism designed to bypass Western dollar networks by allowing India and Iran to trade using their respective domestic currencies.
This refers to actions by a central bank, like the RBI, to influence the exchange rate of its currency. It often involves buying or selling foreign currency to manage supply and demand in the market.
A gas turbine engine optimized to produce shaft power rather than jet thrust, commonly used to drive helicopter rotors.
A collaborative digital platform where developers publicly share, modify, and collaborate on software code and machine learning models.
The process of converting state-owned public assets into new sources of revenue through disinvestments, leases, or strategic sales.
Residential properties priced within a specific range, historically below ₹45 lakh in India, designed to serve lower-to-middle income buyers.
A commercial arrangement in which two or more independent business entities agree to pool their resources to accomplish a specific technical or market objective.
A type of hydroelectric generation facility where little or no water storage is provided, relying instead on the natural flow of the river to generate electricity.
A digital marketplace that enables advertisers and publishers to buy and sell advertising space through real-time bidding.
A decision made by an impartial third party (an arbitrator or arbitration panel) in a dispute, which is legally binding on both parties involved, similar to a court judgment.
A credit rating that assesses the creditworthiness of a country, indicating the risk level for investors. It influences a nation's borrowing costs on international markets.
The profit a company makes from its core business operations before deducting interest and taxes. It's a key measure of how efficiently a company is managing its main activities.
Loans raised by eligible resident entities from recognised non-resident entities, typically used to fund large projects or expand business operations overseas.
A set of open, interoperable technology platforms and standards provided by governments to enable services like digital payments (e.g., UPI) and identity verification.
Financial transactions where the payer and the receiver are in different countries. Efforts aim to make these faster, cheaper, and more transparent using digital technology.
The processing capability of computers, especially relevant for complex tasks like Artificial Intelligence. It refers to the speed and capacity to perform calculations and data operations.
A legal proceeding in which a group of people with similar financial grievances collectively sue a corporate defendant, often used by public shareholders to seek damages.
A government-maintained fund used to purchase essential commodities directly during high-supply periods and release them during shortages to regulate retail market prices.
A financial term referring to the percentage write-off that creditors agree to accept during a debt settlement or corporate bankruptcy resolution.
Highly regulated institutional investors like mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds that have the expertise and financial strength to evaluate large capital market issues.
A leverage service offered by stockbrokers allowing investors to buy shares by paying a fraction of the total value as collateral and borrowing the rest at interest.
Long-term investment capital where the investor is willing to wait many years for a return, typical of pension funds backing infrastructure.
A real-time estimate of a stock or index's price during an auction window, which can fluctuate wildly before the final price settles.
An alliance where a technology company and a licensed bank jointly issue a financial product, combining tech distribution with regulated banking licenses.
Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement, a treaty between two countries to protect and encourage foreign investments.
A method of sending digital data over long distances using light signals through fiber-optic cables.
A state of financial distress where a person or company cannot pay their debts as they become due.
A data centre is a facility used to house computer systems and associated components, such as telecommunications and storage systems, for data processing and storage.
4G refers to the fourth generation of broadband cellular network technology, offering significantly faster mobile internet speeds than its predecessors, 2G and 3G.

A company repurchasing its own shares from the open market, often to boost shareholder value by reducing the number of outstanding shares or to consolidate ownership, indicating confidence in its future.
Specialized financial services offered by banks to high-net-worth individuals, including wealth management, investment advice, and personalized banking solutions, focusing on affluent clients.
A private startup company valued at over $1 billion. This term signifies rapid growth and significant market potential in the venture capital industry.
When an entity, like a bank or government, borrows money by issuing debt securities (bonds) to investors. Investors receive regular interest payments, and their principal back at maturity.
Indian financial institutions, such as mutual funds, insurance companies, and banks, that invest in the domestic stock market, reflecting local market sentiment.
Assets held by a central bank in foreign currencies. These reserves are crucial for managing exchange rates, facilitating international trade, and acting as a buffer during economic shocks.
A system where specific nutritional warnings (e.g., high sugar, salt, fat) are placed prominently on the front of food packaging to help consumers make healthier choices quickly.

An economic indicator that measures the changes in the volume of production of industrial products over a specific period. It reflects the health of the manufacturing, mining, and electricity sectors.
A key economic indicator that measures the short-term changes in the volume of electricity, mining, and manufacturing goods produced in an economy compared to a baseline period.

term: BIPPA (Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement)
definition: A treaty between two nations designed to protect and promote foreign investments by establishing clear legal guidelines, fair treatment, and dispute resolution mechanisms.
The basic units of information in quantum computing, equivalent to bits in classical computing, capable of representing a 0, a 1, or both simultaneously due to quantum physics.
A government policy through which the state regulates and caps the retail price of critical energy commodities like domestic natural gas to protect consumers from market volatility.
A class of prescription drugs in India that cannot be purchased over the counter without a written prescription from a registered medical practitioner.
A nutrition labeling system that places clear, simplified nutritional warnings or ratings on the front of food packaging to help consumers make quick health decisions.
An invitation to existing shareholders to purchase additional new shares in a company at a discounted price, used to raise fresh capital.
The illegal transfer of corporate funds, assets, or capital by promoters or executives for personal use or unauthorized sister entities.
